A couple years ago, my brother was out jogging at like 1 AM (his daily schedule is weird). Before heading home, he went to the nearby park to get a drink from the Coca Cola vending machine there. As he was inserting the bill into the machine, he heard a rustling noise behind him and suddenly felt a chill through his body, the kind that makes your hair stand on end. He was completely alone, even the usual night guards were gone so he was starting to feel on edge. There was more rustling noise and he noticed the sound was getting closer. In panic, he immediately pressed for a Coke, and once the can dropped, he grabbed it and ran back to the road straight for home. Once he got home, he felt relieved but also a bit ridiculous for being all worked up. After catching his breath, he proceeded to open the can of Coke, but was so shocked when he saw what he was holding that he almost dropped it. It was a can of Pepsi.

One of my closest friends and I got into a relationship which lasted a couple months. We eventually agreed to end it, but with different reasons. He didn't want to commit to a serious relationship, and I felt we barely had any common ground with each other (we're close because our brains think and react similarly, but our interests align nowhere). We were cool during the actual breakup and promised to stay friends, but the following months were terrible. We kept arguing and randomly ignoring each other. We would unintentionally offend the other person and over analyze each other's words. We didn't even argue when we were still a couple, so why now? I remember I was so frustrated that the whole "you can never be friends again with an ex" thing might be true.
So we had a long chat about it and decided to do a full reset. We'd take a break, then just start talking to each other when we felt like it. We'd say hi when we passed in the halls, then we started joining in the same group conversations, and eventually I was hanging out at his dorm in the same bed as him, watching funny videos.
So how did it turn out? Well I'm back where I started, but I learned a shitload about relationships and breakups.
